subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw implement a guard-only read-tool fallback for known binary documents now, or wait for broader document extraction/provider-native file handling?
rationale: Current main still has the token-waste path, but the issue proposes both a lightweight guard and automatic parsing, and the linked PR candidate is stale/conflicting against older file names.

options.title: Adopt guard-only fallback
options.body: Implement the safe default in the current read tool and tests, with PDF users directed to the existing pdf tool and Office extraction tracked separately.

options.title: Fold into broader document work
options.body: Keep this issue as a narrower child of provider-native/document ingestion work and avoid a one-off read-tool guard until the larger design lands.

options.title: Refresh the linked PR first
options.body: Ask the linked fork PR author to retarget current files and provide proof before deciding whether to adopt or replace the branch.

recommendation.title: Adopt guard-only fallback
recommendation.body: Implement the safe default in the current read tool and tests, with PDF users directed to the existing pdf tool and Office extraction tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc recently maintained the Office/read path normalization and inbound media-read boundary most directly related to this choice.
